sections.overview: This forester moth is a member of Jordanita, a genus of day-flying Zygaenidae with disjunct European and Asian populations.
sections.identification: Metallic green adults can resemble related Jordanita; expert accounts warn that reliable identification may require genital examination.
sections.habitat: It favours open steppe and dry, rocky, low-nutrient grassland, from lowlands to mountain slopes.
sections.diet: The leaf-mining larvae feed on Asteraceae; French records report Centaurea leucophaea and Artemisia alba as hosts.
sections.behavior: Species-level behavioral observations are sparse in the specialist accounts consulted; adults are recorded locally in spring.
sections.reproduction: Larvae mine host-plant leaves; a genus-level study reports overwintering as larvae for most Jordanita species, not specifically this moth.
sections.ecology: Unlike the broader-habitat J. globulariae, J. budensis is a dry-steppe specialist; the two share the genus but differ ecologically.
sections.conservation: It is rare in western and central Europe; a global Red List category was not verified in the sources used.
